questions.question: Describe the Karoo and explain why it is good for sheep farming but not for crops.
questions.expected_answer: The Karoo is a very dry semi-desert with hot summers, cold winters, little rain and small tough bushes instead of much grass. Sheep can eat the bushes, but crops cannot grow without irrigation because there is too little rain.

questions.question: How do Karoo farmers get water for their sheep?
questions.expected_answer: They drill boreholes to reach water under the ground. Windmills or solar pumps pump the water up into reservoirs, and it flows through pipes to troughs.

questions.question: Why are Karoo farms so large, and why do farmers move sheep between camps?
questions.expected_answer: Each sheep needs a large area of veld to find enough bushes to eat, so the farms must be very large. Farmers move sheep between camps so the bushes can grow back and the veld is not overgrazed.
